# fjordrun_deployment (Resource)

An explicit deployment of a service (or function) in one environment. Fjordrun resources save changes without deploying by default, so this is how an apply rolls out: one deployment per service per apply, after everything it depends on is in place.

A new deployment starts when the resource is created and whenever `triggers` changes. Build `triggers` from whatever should cause a rollout: the service's `config_hash`, the variables' `variables_hash`, an image tag or a Git commit SHA.

Deployments are history: destroying this resource leaves the service running as it is, unless `remove_on_destroy` is set.

## Example Usage

```terraform
variable "team_id" {
  type = string
}

resource "fjordrun_project" "shop" {
  team_id = var.team_id
  name    = "shop"
}

resource "fjordrun_service" "web" {
  project_id     = fjordrun_project.shop.id
  environment_id = fjordrun_project.shop.default_environment_id
  name           = "web"
  source         = { type = "image", image = "nginxdemos/hello:0.4" }
}

resource "fjordrun_service_variables" "web" {
  service_id     = fjordrun_service.web.id
  environment_id = fjordrun_service.web.environment_id
  variables      = { LOG_LEVEL = "info" }
}

resource "fjordrun_volume" "web" {
  service_id     = fjordrun_service.web.id
  environment_id = fjordrun_service.web.environment_id
  mount_path     = "/data"
}

# One deployment per apply, after everything above, whenever any of these changes.
resource "fjordrun_deployment" "web" {
  service_id     = fjordrun_service.web.id
  environment_id = fjordrun_service.web.environment_id
  wait           = true

  triggers = {
    config    = fjordrun_service.web.config_hash
    variables = fjordrun_service_variables.web.variables_hash
    volume    = fjordrun_volume.web.id
  }

  timeouts = {
    create = "20m"
    update = "20m"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `environment_id` (String) Environment ID.
- `service_id` (String) Service or function ID.

### Optional

- `remove_on_destroy` (Boolean) Remove the deployment when this resource is destroyed, which stops the service if it is the active one.
- `timeouts` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--timeouts))
- `triggers` (Map of String) Any change to this map starts a new deployment.
- `wait` (Boolean) Wait until the deployment finishes, up to the `create`/`update` timeout (default 30 minutes), and fail the apply unless it succeeds.

### Read-Only

- `commit_sha` (String) The commit, for GitHub sources.
- `created_at` (String) Creation time.
- `finished_at` (String) When it finished.
- `id` (String) ID of the latest deployment this resource started.
- `image` (String) The deployed image.
- `is_active` (Boolean) Whether this deployment is the one serving the service.
- `status` (String) `queued`, `building`, `deploying`, `success`, `failed`, `crashed`, `cancelled`, `skipped` or `removed`. A later deployment moves an old one to `removed`: this is not a diff.
- `trigger` (String) What the API records as the cause.

<a id="nestedatt--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
- `update` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# by deployment ID. Triggers aren't known to the API: the next apply with triggers deploys once.
terraform import fjordrun_deployment.web 12121212-1212-1212-1212-121212121212
```
